english.title: Deportation / removal - fail to take action as required by Secretary of State

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Asylum and Immigration Treatment of Claimants etc Act 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed without reasonable excuse to comply with a requirement of the Secretary of State made under section 35(1) of the Asylum and Immigration (Treatment of Claimants, etc.) Act 2004, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REQUIREMENT..), which would or may have enabled a travel document to be obtained by or for you, the possession of which would have facilitated your deportation or removal from the United Kingdom
english.legislation: Contrary to section 35(3) and (4) of the Asylum and Immigration (Treatment of Claimants, etc.) Act 2004.

english.notes:
Subsection 35(2) provides that the Secretary of State may require a person to -
(a) provide information or documents to the Secretary of State or to any other person;
(b) obtain information or documents;
(c) provide fingerprints, submit to the taking of a photograph or provide information, or submit to a process for the recording of information, about external physical characteristics (including, in particular, features of the iris or any other part of the eye);
(d) make, or consent to or cooperate with the making of, an application to a person acting for the government of a State other than the United Kingdom;
(e) cooperate with a process designed to enable determination of an application;
(f) complete a form accurately and completely;
(g) attend an interview and answer questions accurately and completely;
(h) make an appointment.

other.penalty:
Either way

Summary: maximum 6/ 12 months imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit on prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(4)(b) of the Asylum and Immigration (Treatment of Claimants, etc.) Act 2004 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
